newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end higher led by mining sector.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end higher led by mining sector.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Wednesday for the fifth consecutive session, led by the mining sector, which was made attractive by elevated international metal prices, brokers said.
The market would likely continue climbing Thursday as the country's economic growth prospects were healthy, they added.
On Wednesday, the General Index rose 0.17 percent to 1,720.16 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.31 percent to 2,495.67 points.
In a total of 2,025 trades, volume was 45.0 million soles (17.0 million), according to preliminary figures.
"The mining sector is strong. International sales make you think the companies' financial results will be good," said Luis Calderon of local brokerage Acciones y Valores.
Tin miner Minsur climbed 3.93 percent to 10.85 soles on volume of 157,000 shares. Miner Morococha rose 0.77 percent to 2.62 soles on volume of 393,000 shares.

Polymetal miner Atacocha, which reported Wednesday its 1996 net loss narrowed to 3.00 million soles compared with a 19.54 million sol loss in 1995, underperformed the sector, falling 0.9 percent to 1.10 soles in volume of 580,000 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed up 0.62 percent at 6.53 soles in volume of 1.8 million shares.
